key_insight: Bounding initial transverse generator amplitudes reduces noise fragility, while full-width initialization learns faster coherently but stalls on plateaus where coherent and noise-induced gradients cancel.
engineering_relevance: Initialization offers a practical lever for reducing noisy optimization cost without requiring longitudinal disorder or repeated Floquet layers.
method: Study deep variational circuits for a periodic Heisenberg chain under local gate depolarization.
Compare full-width initialization with confined transverse-generator initialization.
Relate fault-erasure fraction to effective visibility using a parameter-free exponential model.
evidence_signal: Full-width circuits require roughly an order of magnitude more updates for noisy convergence, although all tested initializations eventually reach the same fault-erasure fraction and noisy-error band.
watch_item: The findings concern a specific spin-chain setting and local depolarizing noise; transfer to hardware noise and other circuit architectures needs validation.
paper_title: Initialization-controlled fault sensitivity and force-balance plateaus in noisy variational quantum optimization
